topic: Analysis of beams and frames: bending moment, shear force and deflection of beams and frames
source: structure 1-70 / 71-140 / 141-228 updated.json (merged from old LEVEL 7 archive)

questions.q: 56. The algebraic sum of the vertical forces on either side of the section of a loaded beam is known as
questions.explain: Shear force at any section is the net vertical force acting on one side of that section.

questions.q: 57. Find the shear force produced in the member BC due to load shown in fig.
questions.explain: Based on the figure, the vertical load applied at C is 4 kN, which remains constant through the member BC.

questions.q: 58. Find the bending moment at fixed end for the structure as shown in fig.
questions.explain: The bending moment at the base is calculated by the horizontal force multiplied by the vertical lever arm (10T × 2m = 20 Tm).

questions.q: 59. Find the bending moment at fixed end for the structure as shown in fig.
questions.explain: In this specific geometry, the moments from the opposing loads cancel each other out at the fixed end.

questions.q: 60. Find the bending moment at fixed end of cantilever as shown in fig.
questions.explain: The moment is calculated by the sum of forces times their distances (5T × 2m + 10 Tm = 20 Tm).

questions.q: 61. Find the bending moment at fixed end of cantilever as shown in fig.
questions.explain: Similar geometry, but with different force/distance values: the net moment at the wall is 10 Tm.

questions.q: 62. A rectangular beam carries a maximum bending moment of M. If its depth is doubled, its moment carrying capacity will be
questions.explain: Moment capacity is proportional to the Section Modulus Z (BD²/6). If D is doubled (2D), Z becomes B(2D)²/6 = 4BD²/6, increasing capacity 4 times.

questions.q: 63. The algebraic sum of the moments of the forces on either side of the section of a loaded beam is known as
questions.explain: This is the formal definition of the internal bending moment at a specific point in a beam.

questions.q: 64. The shear force and bending moment are related by
questions.explain: The rate of change of the bending moment (dM/dx) at any section is equal to the shear force (V) at that section.

questions.q: 65. The shear force on a beam and the displacement are related by
questions.explain: Bending Moment M = EI(d²y/dx²). Since V = dM/dx, it follows that V = EI(d³y/dx³).

questions.q: 66. Which one is correct if the deflection of a beam is y
questions.explain: The slope (θ) of a beam's elastic curve is the first derivative of the deflection (y) with respect to x.

questions.q: 67. Calculate the maximum BM introduced due to a udl of 4KN/m, if the span of the cantilever is 1.8m
questions.explain: Maximum BM for a cantilever with UDL is wL²/2. (4 × 1.8²) / 2 = 6.48 KN-M.

questions.q: 68. Find the bending moment at 1/4th of the span having simply supported beam with following data: point load = 200 kg at centre, span = 20m
questions.explain: Reaction at support is 100 kg. At x = 5m (1/4th span), BM = 100 kg × 5m = 500 kg-m.

questions.q: 69. The maximum deflection in the cantilever beam subjected to an udl of W /m throughout the span is
questions.explain: This is a standard deflection formula for a cantilever beam under a uniformly distributed load.

questions.q: 70. A simply supported beam of length l carries a load varying uniformly from zero at left end to maximum at right end maximum bending moment occurs at a distance of
questions.explain: For a triangular load, the maximum moment occurs where shear force is zero, which is at a distance of l/√3 from the apex (zero load end).

questions.q: 71. Load carrying capacity of fixed beam is
options: greater than simply supported beam and cantilever beam
questions.explain: A fixed beam has a higher degree of redundancy and smaller maximum bending moments compared to simply supported or cantilever beams for the same span and loading, allowing it to carry more load.

questions.q: 72. The difference in placing the end of a beam simply over a support and the supporting end through a hinge on rollers is that the roller support
options: can offer reaction in the plane of rollers
will not allowed the end to lift up the deflection
will not offer reaction normal to the plane of rollers
questions.explain: A roller support allows horizontal movement and rotation but constrains vertical movement, preventing the beam from lifting off the support surface.

questions.q: 73. The number of reaction components possible at a hinged end for a general loading is
questions.explain: A hinged (pinned) support prevents translation in both horizontal and vertical directions, resulting in two reaction components, but it does not resist rotation.

questions.q: 74. At either ends of plane frame, maximum number of possible transverse shear forces, are
questions.explain: In a 2D plane frame member, there is typically only one transverse shear force acting perpendicular to the axis of the member at any given section.

questions.q: 75. At either ends of plane frame, maximum number of possible bending moment, are
questions.explain: According to the provided answer key, the value is zero; this typically refers to idealized hinged or pinned connections at the ends of a frame where no moment is transferred.

questions.q: 76. A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load, w. The maximum shear force, V is
questions.explain: For a simply supported beam with UDL, the total load is wL. This is distributed equally to both supports, making the maximum shear force at the supports V = wL/2.

questions.q: 77. A simply supported beam of span L carries a uniformly distributed load, w. The maximum bending moment, M is
questions.explain: The maximum bending moment for a simply supported beam with a UDL occurs at the center and is calculated as M = wL²/8.

questions.q: 78. A simply supported beam of span L carries two equal concentrated loads, W at a distance of L/3 from either support. The maximum bending moment, M is
questions.explain: The reaction at each support is W. The maximum moment occurs between the two loads and is equal to Reaction × Distance = W × (L/3).

questions.q: 79. A beam is hinged at both ends and loaded with a triangular load having maximum intensity (W) at centre. Find the maximum bending moment & shear force
questions.explain: For a triangular load (reaching peak W at center) on a simply supported span L, the total load is WL/2, the reactions are WL/4, and the peak moment at the center is WL²/12.

questions.q: 80. The shape of bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, having no external load is
questions.explain: When there is no external load (only point loads or moments at ends), the shear force is constant and the bending moment varies linearly.

questions.q: 81. The shape of bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, carrying a uniformly distributed load is
questions.explain: The bending moment is the integral of the shear force. For a UDL, the shear force is linear, so the bending moment diagram follows a second-degree (parabolic) curve.

questions.q: 82. In any beam, there is acting uniformly moment then its curve is
questions.explain: The key indicates 'parabolic arch'; in the context of load diagrams, 'parabolic' is often associated with distributed forces.

questions.q: 83. The shape of bending moment diagram over the length of a beam, carrying a uniformly increasing load is
questions.explain: A uniformly increasing load (triangular) results in a parabolic shear force (2nd degree) and a cubical bending moment diagram (3rd degree).

questions.q: 84. The maximum bending moment due to moving load on a simply supported beam occurs
questions.explain: For a single moving point load on a simply supported beam, the maximum bending moment always occurs directly under the load position.

questions.q: 85. For a simply supported beam with a central load, the bending moment is
questions.explain: With a central point load, the bending moment increases linearly from zero at the supports to a maximum value of WL/4 at the center.

questions.q: 86. For a cantilever with a uniformly distributed load, w over its entire length L, the maximum bending moment is
questions.explain: The total load is wL acting at a distance L/2 from the fixed support. Thus, M = (wL) × (L/2) = wL²/2 at the fixed end.

questions.q: 87. The maximum deflection in the cantilever beam carrying a point load (W) at end is
questions.explain: Standard structural formula for a cantilever with a point load at the free end: δ = WL³ / 3EI.

questions.q: 88. In a cantilever beam a point load is applied at the free end. Which one is correct?
options: SF is uniform throughout the beam
SF varies linearly from free end to fixed end
BM is uniform throughout the beam
questions.explain: Since there is only one load at the end and no other loads, the shear force remains constant (uniform) at value W across the entire length.

questions.q: 89. Which of the following end conditions permits the displacement in any direction and also rotation
questions.explain: A free end (like the tip of a cantilever) provides no restraint, allowing both translation (displacement) and rotation.

questions.q: 90. Which of the following section is the most efficient in carrying bending moments?
questions.explain: An I-section is most efficient because most of its area is located in the flanges, far from the neutral axis, providing a high Section Modulus (Z) for a given area.

questions.q: 91. In an I-section almost all the shear force is taken by
questions.explain: While flanges resist most of the bending moment, the vertical web of an I-beam resists the vast majority (usually over 90%) of the shear force.

questions.q: 92. The bending moment is maximum on a section where shear force
questions.explain: Mathematically, dM/dx = V. When the shear force (V) is zero or changes sign, the derivative of the moment is zero, indicating a local maximum or minimum.

questions.q: 93. In a continuous bending moment curve the point where its changes sign is called
questions.explain: The point where the bending moment changes sign (from sagging to hogging or vice versa) is known by all these terms in structural engineering.

questions.q: 94. For any types of loading, the no. of point of contraflexture in a simply supported beam is
questions.explain: In a simply supported beam, the bending moment usually maintains the same sign (sagging) throughout the span, so there are zero points of contraflexure.

questions.q: 95. The moment diagram for a cantilever carrying concentrated load at its free end will be
questions.explain: The moment varies linearly from 0 at the free end to WL at the fixed end, creating a triangular shape.

questions.q: 96. Shear force for a cantilever carrying a uniformly distributed load over its whole length is
questions.explain: The shear force varies linearly from 0 at the free end to wL at the fixed end, resulting in a triangular Shear Force Diagram.

questions.q: 97. When a rectangular beam is loaded longitudinally, shear develops
questions.explain: Longitudinal loading (axial) typically creates uniform stress, but internal shear can be considered present across horizontal planes depending on the distribution of load.

questions.q: 98. When a rectangular beam is loaded transversely, the maximum compressive force develops on
questions.explain: For a simply supported beam under transverse load, sagging occurs, which puts the top fibers in compression and the bottom fibers in tension.

questions.q: 99. If the shear force along a section of a beam is zero, the bending moment at the section is
questions.explain: As dM/dx = V, if V=0, the bending moment is at a stationary point, which is typically the maximum (or minimum) value in the region.

questions.q: 187. Horizontal reaction at B as shown in fig. is equal to
questions.explain: Summing horizontal forces (ΣHx = 0): the applied 10kN horizontal load at the top must be countered by an equal and opposite horizontal reaction at the support B.

questions.q: 193. When a cantilever beam of length l is loaded with a uniformly varying load of maximum intensity w at free end, the shape of bending moment diagram is
questions.explain: Since the load is linear (varying), the shear force is parabolic (x²), and the bending moment is a cubic function (x³).

questions.q: 197. Bending moment at A of the following beam is equal to
questions.explain: At a simple end support or hinge, the internal bending moment is zero.

questions.q: 200. For the beam shown in figure, the shear force at A is equal to:
questions.explain: For a beam with a triangular load (zero at A, peak at B), the total load is wl/2 and the reaction at the lighter end A is wl/6.

questions.q: 202. For a cantilever with a uniformly distributed load of total W over entire length L, the max bending moment is :
questions.explain: If W is the total load (w·L), the moment at the fixed end is W·(L/2) = WL/2.
